To synchronize with Node using the Physics process, the Modifier update process in Skeleton should be Physics as well.

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ccdbe6ff-f271-4bde-bb05-c382aac2dbed)

Thanks for the response @TokageItLab Enabling that results in this behavior when at a low physics rate:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/86507b5d-1f65-4267-be9a-a1b4aed2b761

And at 60 physics ticks, the IK is still very jittery:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/eab403c8-ea99-4ee7-b4e7-86a22ea49161

I see, so there are two out-of-sync behaviors in the video in the description.

- "Idle" vs "Physics" Process
- "Interpolated" vs "Non-interpolated" Physics result

Regarding the former, as I commented above, the synchronization gap between Physics Process and Idle Process can be solved by setting the Modifier's CallbackModeProcess to Physics. When the FPS is low, it seems to be reduced, but actually, the latter synchronization gap is still left.

The current process order looks like this:

1. Skeleton3D's _physics_process to make a flag to deferred update 
2. iterate SkeletonModifiers in skeleton deferred update process
3. PhysicalServer's physics interpolation

However, ideally, the process should be done in the following order:

1. Skeleton3D's _physics_process to make a flag to deferred update 
2. PhysicalServer's physics interpolation
3. iterate SkeletonModifiers in skeleton deferred update process

Any good ideas on how to resolve this @lawnjelly ?

I don't know the details of how Physics Interpolation is implemented. However, if the Physics Interpolation is done in conjunction with the RenderingServer, I would think we could do something within the RenderingServer. If not so, I guess it might require some additional processing for the Skeleton's Physics Process to wait for Physics Interpolation to be processed.

Just taking a look.

First thing (which isn't really related to the behaviour your are seeing) is that for your `Camera` script, you are pointing to the correct documentation, but you don't need to do all that stuff yourself (storing previous and current xforms of the target, and interpolating), it can be done automatically for you by calling the helper function `get_global_transform_interpolated()`.

So you just need a one-liner:
```
func _process(_delta):
	global_position = target.get_global_transform_interpolated().origin
```
That's literally it, providing you have turned interpolation off (`set_physics_interpolation_mode(Node.PHYSICS_INTERPOLATION_MODE_OFF)` or in the inspector).

Indeed your method for updating prev and curr xforms looks to have bugs (I don't think it will work if two physics ticks occur before a frame), which is why using the in-built method is advised, aside from being less verbose etc.

Ok I have a workaround for now, add this script to `Skeleton3D` (and keep it in idle mode):

```
extends Skeleton3D

func _ready() -> void:
	set_as_top_level(true)
	physics_interpolation_mode = Node.PHYSICS_INTERPOLATION_MODE_OFF
	
func _process(delta: float) -> void:
	global_transform = get_parent().get_global_transform_interpolated()
```

This is presumably also a problem in 3.x, I only tested the IK with the Godot IK demo which had a non-moving root node.

I figured out IK works most sensibly when kept in idle mode, with physics interpolation OFF for the skeleton, the only difference is that the target should be client interpolated, so in the c++ code it calls `get_global_transform_interpolated()` for the target. And it works great when the root node of the skeleton is not moving.

When moving, the problem is that the skeleton root will jump on each physics tick if physics interpolation is off. So we actually want the `Skeleton3D` itself to be interpolated, but the bones to be non-interpolated. There's no easy shortcut for this in the inspector, which is why I've done it in a script above (turned off interpolation in the `Skeleton3D` and hence all its bone children, and manually interpolated the `Skeleton3D` itself).

I'll look at a PR to do this automagically - I'll probably look at this after the weekend as there are some deeper considerations as `Skeleton3D` is shared for a number of different areas - including animation, IK and ragdoll .. so needs to work well with all (and modifications for one can cause regressions in another).

_As an aside, it is also possible theoretically to run the IK totally on the physics tick, but because interpolation is approximate, that means on the in betweener frames the IK will not line up exactly with the target, and it will appear as subtle jitter, which is why I thought it better to standardize on running the IK on the frame. Particle systems are also a similar exception, where it is often better to run them without physics interpolation._
Btw, I have a similar problem with a Skeleton2D. Unfortunately, there is no `get_global_transform_interpolated()` in 2D, so the trick above doesn't apply.

> Btw, I have a similar problem with a Skeleton2D. Unfortunately, there is no `get_global_transform_interpolated()` in 2D, so the trick above doesn't apply.

2D will need its own issue .. it's related, but physics interpolation works very differently in 2D, transform traversal is done server side in 2D, in 3D it is done client side in the scene tree and only global xforms are uploaded to the server.

Hey , thanks for this this has fixed some issues for me!

while this works perfectly fine for a fixed camera related to the characterbody itself, I'm trying to get the position of the head bone in real time but I get the same delay that's there without your fix.

I tried using a BoneAttachment3D to the head bone, didn't work.

I also tried adding this to the skeleton script
	global_transform = get_parent().get_global_transform_interpolated()
	
	var bone_idx : int = skeleton.find_bone("Head")
	force_update_bone_child_transform(bone_idx)
	var local_bone_transform : Transform3D = skeleton.get_bone_global_pose(bone_idx)
	var global_bone_pos : Vector3 = skeleton.to_global(local_bone_transform.origin)
	head_position = global_bone_pos
then I tried updating the value on_skeleton_update but I had the same exact issue on all three solutions. (Mesh moving faster than the camera itself lagging behind)

and lastly I also tried by lerping from a fixed point to the head position but the position are too far from the actual visual position of the head so this makes it really jerky..

I must be doing something wrong or this is just something that's not possible with interpolation?

I'm currently looking at changing the architecture for 3D interpolation to make this kind of problem easier by doing the interpolation scene tree side rather than server side, I'm just working on this (I'll be posting a WIP PR for 3.x very soon, and it can be forward ported to 4.x). The problems here are common to ragdoll, IK and XR.

So any fixes here may be out of date soon.

I think the generic problem with IK is that the chain roots have to be set to read interpolated xforms in the code rather than physics xforms, and I'm not quite sure where that is done yet in the `SkeletonIK` stuff, am investigating. 👍 

Yeah can confirm the solution in the IK demo when I add root motion, as in the workaround, is to set the `Skeleton` to `top_level`, interpolation off, and `get_global_transform_interpolated()` from the parent. The IK chains seem to use the `Skeleton` `global_transform` as the coordinate space for the bone global poses which are used as the chain roots.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b1aefaef-e77e-4dec-9810-da8f3fea4164

(This video is with the new scene side physics interpolation)

That looks promising! I'll just put IK on hold and ignore the visual glitches for now and hope this gets added in a future release.

For the record, I managed to fix my bone attachment camera issue by adding the Camera directly under the BoneAttachment3D in the hierarchy with IK disabled (which is already the case with the skeleton code script anyway) and moving the camera (still as a top level node)  using get_parent().get_global_transform() in process

For some reason putting the camera in the actual skeleton hierarchy fixed my issue and I went from having a huge positional difference to basically none;

But then I tried setting my animationtree process back to idle mode because my animations looked sluggish without it and it replaced the positional issue with "shakiness" issue

There's no fps arms here the upperbody is rotated towards the camera using IK

Everything working as it should (ignore the left arm which is another IK that's confliting with the one aiming the upperbody)

And with animationtree on idle

As you can see here when i'm moving the arms are visually shaking but it's actually the camera that can't get the proper position for some reason

Worth nothing that even if I disable every IK I still get the shakiness issue (Both on Jolt and default physics engine) so it's not related to IK 

My solution so far has been to set physics to 120 steps and keep my animationtree in physics mode but i'm not sure if it's ideal and the animations will still be low fps on 240hz monitor and more. I've finally found the cause of the need for the IK to have the skeleton in interpolated space:

In FabrikInverseKinematic::solve (probably same for other solvers:
```
make_goal(p_task, p_task->skeleton->get_global_transform().affine_inverse(), blending_delta);
```
IK runs every frame, and it was getting the global_transform in physics space.

If we change this to the following, we can get the skeleton transform in interpolated space, _without_ running the scripting workaround:
```
make_goal(p_task, p_task->skeleton->get_global_transform_interpolated().affine_inverse(), blending_delta);
```
This seems on the face of it a better longterm solution for the engine for IK, as there are no user changes required, it should *just work* :tm: .

Can't guarantee this is the way to go yet as there are a number of reported bugs to sort in IK etc, but it looks promising. 👍
